# Dev Quartz operating record

The Dev Quartz team introduced this record after two review cycles exposed inconsistent handling of routine requests. The coordinator assigns each case to a named operator, logs the intake date, and checks whether the request belongs to the shared workflow. The process is designed for ordinary weekday operations and preserves the original request when a later correction is needed. A reviewer can return an incomplete case to the coordinator without changing its recorded decision date.

The operating decision is applied as follows. The adopted Dev Quartz rule requires 2 checks and records the decision receipt. Operators record the actor, target, measurement, and time window in the case log before taking action. The duty lead reviews the log at the end of the shift and records either acceptance, a correction, or a reason that the case must wait. This separation keeps a proposed change from silently becoming the rule used by the next operator.

When the normal path cannot run, the operator pauses the case, names the missing dependency, and contacts the duty lead through the documented escalation channel. A replacement operator reads the case log before resuming and records what was checked. If an error is found after action, the team preserves the first record, adds a correction entry, and replays only the affected step. A reviewer may approve a recovery during the same business day, but recovery does not erase the original event.

The record also covers handoff and review. The coordinator keeps the responsible queue visible, while the reviewer checks that the stated actor and scope match the request.
